claim: For positive integers \(d,q\), let \(\mu(d,q)\) be the least positive integer \(N\) for which there exists a complex matrix \(T\in M_N(\mathbb C)\) with power-quasinormality index set \(\mathcal{PQ}(T)=\{d(q+k):k\in\mathbb N_0\}\), where \(\mathcal{PQ}(T)=\{n\in\mathbb N:[T^n,T^*T]=0\}\). Then \[\mu(1,1)=1,\qquad \mu(1,q)=q\ (q\ge2),\qquad \mu(d,1)=2\ (d\ge2),\qquad \mu(d,q)=(q-1)d+3\ (d,q\ge2).\] For \(d,q\ge2\), the upper bound is attained by \(S_d\oplus J_{(q-1)d+1}\), where \(\mathcal{PQ}(S_d)=d\mathbb N\) and \(J_r\) is the nilpotent Jordan block of order \(r\). The lower bound follows by decomposing any finite-dimensional realization at its first power-quasinormal exponent \(dq\) into an invertible periodic sector and a nilpotent sector: the periodic sector has dimension at least \(2\) when \(d>1\), while exclusion of \((q-1)d\) forces the nilpotent sector to have dimension at least \((q-1)d+1\).
scientific_limitations: Restricted to finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces (complex matrices).
Determines the minimum dimension but does not classify all minimizers up to unitary similarity.
An older equivalent statement under n-power-normal terminology remains a residual literature risk despite targeted searches.
title: Exact minimal dimensions for power-quasinormality index sets
